original_question: Fix r >= 1 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is a B_{2,r+1}-free non-bipartite graph with m edges, is it true that lambda(G) is at most rho(m, r), where rho(m, r) is the largest root of x^3 - x^2 - (m - 1)x + m - 2r - 1 = 0, with equality exactly when m == 1 mod r and G is isomorphic to K^+_{r,(m-1)/r}?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Conjecture 3.8, the survey’s proposed answer to Problem 6 for B_{2,r+1}-free non-bipartite graphs with m edges. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core content of the paper’s Conjecture 3.8: the parameters r ≥ 1 and sufficiently large m, the class of B_{2,r+1}-free non-bipartite graphs with m edges, the bound λ(G) ≤ ρ(m,r) defined by the cubic x^3 − x^2 − (m−1)x + m − 2r − 1, and the equality case m ≡ 1 (mod r) with extremal graph K^+_{r,(m−1)/r}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))
missing_details: The ambient setting is implicit: the paper works with finite, undirected, simple graphs. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))
λ(G) should be defined explicitly as the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix A(G). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))

B_{2,r+1} should be defined as the book graph K_2 ∨ (r+1)K_1, equivalently the graph obtained from K_{2,r+1} by adding an edge joining the two vertices of degree r+1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))
K^+_{a,b} should be defined as the graph obtained from K_{a,b} by adding an edge inside the part of size b. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))

“m is sufficiently large” should be quantified as: there exists an integer M(r) (or m_0(r)) depending only on r such that the statement holds for all m ≥ M(r); the paper does not specify this threshold. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))

The phrase “with m edges” or “with size m” should be made explicit as |E(G)| = m; in the paper’s general notation, 𝒢(m,ℱ) consists of ℱ-free graphs with m edges and no isolated vertices, although isolated vertices are immaterial here. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))

ρ(m,r) should be specified as the largest real root of the stated cubic, and the equality graph K^+_{r,(m−1)/r} is well-defined only when r divides m−1, which is why the congruence condition m ≡ 1 (mod r) must be stated. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))
refined_question: For each integer r ≥ 1, does there exist an integer M(r) such that whenever m ≥ M(r) and G is a finite simple non-bipartite graph with |E(G)| = m that contains no copy of the book graph B_{2,r+1} = K_2 ∨ (r+1)K_1, the spectral radius λ(G) of its adjacency matrix satisfies λ(G) ≤ ρ(m,r), where ρ(m,r) is the largest real root of x^3 − x^2 − (m−1)x + m − 2r − 1 = 0? Moreover, does equality hold if and only if m ≡ 1 (mod r) and G ≅ K^+_{r,(m−1)/r}, where K^+_{a,b} is obtained from the complete bipartite graph K_{a,b} by adding an edge inside the part of size b? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))
justification: The draft is aiming at Conjecture 3.8 rather than merely Problem 6, because the cubic x^3 − x^2 − (m−1)x + m − 2r − 1, the congruence condition m ≡ 1 (mod r), and the extremal candidate K^+_{r,(m−1)/r} uniquely identify that conjecture. The nearby context needed to make the question stand-alone is split between the introduction, where λ(G), A(G), and 𝒢(m,ℱ) are defined, and the beginning of Section 3, where K^+_{a,b} and B_{2,r+1} are defined and Problem 6 is posed. The survey also explains immediately before Conjecture 3.8 that Liu and Miao’s earlier guess K^+_{1,m−1} is not sharp, because K^+_{r,(m−1)/r} is still B_{2,r+1}-free and can have larger spectral radius when m ≡ 1 (mod r) and m ≥ r^2; that is why Conjecture 3.8 is the nearest official formulation matching your draft. No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, or nilpotency data are relevant here, since the statement is purely graph-theoretic. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))
